rows.boundary: ICD6.0r5 requires a valid certificate under the network PKI and checks the Controller certificate Common Name against its UCI. The Certificate Guide distinguishes SDK,local testing,exercise and deployment certificates; deployment follows the deploying authority policy. This establishes source requirements,not installed credentials,verified trust,physical identity,permission for a task or current security certification. Virtual-component UCI suffixes do not imply a separate certificate for every virtual member. CMPT §4.1.2 separately requires date validity and nonrevocation. Its high/mid and low-level signer clauses respectively say ISA-approved and acceptable to the deploying organization. M-0004/L-0011 say ECDSA, while L-0013 is titled ECDSA Algorithm but says ECDH; L-0012 literally says the certificate is at least 384 bits long. These statements remain attributed without a repaired algorithm, inferred key-size field or current cryptographic recommendation. Controller Requirements 6.0r4: Controller registration compares the REQUEST ADD originating UCI with the certificate UCI before authorization. Certificate matching does not prove physical identity, completed certificate trust validation or permission to join.
rows.controller_source_review_boundary: Controller registration compares the REQUEST ADD originating UCI with the certificate UCI before authorization. Certificate matching does not prove physical identity, completed certificate trust validation or permission to join.

rows.boundary: The initiator is the client and the non-initiator is the server for that connection. Controller is a service responsibility and software role; it also has client-side responsibilities. rows.label: Composition member exposure and source attribution
rows.definition: A composition interface component (CIC) exposes composition and member capabilities and determines whether the network sees a member as their source or sees the CIC as their provider.
display: CIC exposes capabilities; visible member retains source attribution; any exposed opaque-member capabilities appear as CIC-provided; visible non-ISA member is virtual

Composition member exposure and source attribution
rows.boundary: Composition is an integration collection, not necessarily a physical assembly. A visible member is announced, has declared capabilities and periodic status; a non-ISA member made visible is a virtual ISA component. Opaque does not mean its capabilities are absent. This is network representation, not independently verified physical provenance or the DMS laser Visible property. CMPT §4.3.15 calls represented non-ISA-interface entities virtual ISA components and requires network announcements/configuration/status/observation handling on their behalf. This strengthens the network-representation interpretation, not physical part-of, independent certificate ownership or direct ISA connectivity. Controller Requirements 6.0r4: When an announcer deregisters or loses connection, still-announced members receive DEVICE REMOVED network notices; this does not prove they were physically disconnected or destroyed.
rows.controller_source_review_boundary: When an announcer deregisters or loses connection, still-announced members receive DEVICE REMOVED network notices; this does not prove they were physically disconnected or destroyed.
rows.controller_final_review_boundary: DEVICE REMOVED leads Live Data to discard retained Config/Status information for the cited participant; that is a service-visible state change, not proof of physical composition change or equipment destruction.

rows.label: Connection-specific network participation lifecycle
rows.definition: A component follows phases of network participation for a Controller connection, with required exchanges and allowed transitions, separately from the continued existence of that connection.
display: Connection → Registration → Configuration → Operational → Deregistration → Disconnection; message-triggered transitions and renewal
Related only · G2-5: Audit subsystem startup/shutdown and service lifecycle requests are separate from ISA connection participation
rows.boundary: The six phases describe ISA participation, not physical asset life, equipment health or command execution. Periodic Status supports communication availability; missing Status does not prove physical failure. Registration renewal, nonresponsive/revived handling, deregistration and connection termination remain distinct; a connection may remain open. Figures illustrate typical and atypical paths, not an invented complete implementation. CMPT distinguishes pre-operational integration, pre-participation discovery/time setup and participation behavior. Its client-side role is the connection initiator; startup connection need is conditional, and connection attempts are at least five seconds apart. M-0032/L-0083–0088 gate Request/Event/Administrative transmission and silently discard early arrivals until the connected peer’s initial Status is received. This initial-Status operational marker remains separately attributed from the SDD initial-Config transition. A permitted IPL data exchange is not automatic permission for every ISA message or proof of hardware readiness. CMPT §4.3.7 adds explicit NON RESPONSIVE and REVIVED recovery exchanges: selected Status within500ms and complete Config within30s. §4.3.16 separately requires resource cleanup and deregistration before leaving; connection termination remains source-qualified because M-0073 says should terminate after Registration Removed while L-0168 says the connection may close and may remain open. Recovery, deregistration and socket closure are not physical asset lifecycle states. Controller Requirements 6.0r4: Controller-specific initial Config/Status deadlines, NON RESPONSIVE/REVIVED, forced REMOVED and mandatory forced connection termination are distinct actor/trigger rules; do not erase differing mid-/low-level time anchors or Component Requirements should/may socket wording.
rows.controller_source_review_boundary: Controller-specific initial Config/Status deadlines, NON RESPONSIVE/REVIVED, forced REMOVED and mandatory forced connection termination are distinct actor/trigger rules; do not erase differing mid-/low-level time anchors or Component Requirements should/may socket wording.
rows.controller_final_review_boundary: DEVICE REMOVED causes Live Data maintained Config/Status cleanup and subscription consumer cleanup; network/cache lifecycle is distinct from physical hardware removal or historical observation deletion.

rows.label: Source-qualified event identity and reference
rows.definition: An event key qualified by its creating component and event time, with an optional reference to an existing event.
display: Event.event ID; Event.event reference → creator + id + time
Related only · G2-5: Audit event types should have identifiers and selected audit events are required
rows.boundary: Not globally unique Event ID alone; do not equate event identity with message identity. CMPT uses Event Reference to connect update and recall Events to a previously published Event. An Event without Event Reference is treated as original; a referenced Event without Recall is an update, and Recall identifies a recall. Preserve this lineage without equating reference with message identity or deleting the cited record.
rows.topics_source_review_boundary: Event Reference targets the original Event fingerprint (normally Time, ID, Source), whereas BSO correlates multiple Events about an observed entity. An illustrative simplified ID column is not an exhaustive native identity schema.

rows.label: Detector property context at event occurrence
rows.definition: Detector-property values at event occurrence, when different from the last Status.
display: Detector property context at event occurrence
rows.boundary: Not every device property, a new sensor, or a guaranteed complete event-time state snapshot. CMPT permits relevant detector-property values that changed since the last Status to accompany an Event and explicitly says this does not count as a Status update. Event context therefore cannot replace the separate Status state-reporting stream.
rows.controller_final_review_boundary: An Event's detector-property values can cause a subscription to start or stop matching without themselves constituting a Status update, actual physical part change or original observation-result provenance.
rows.topics_source_review_boundary: Event Update observables update the augmented event view selectively; unmentioned values persist in the combined interpretation, but Event detector-property context does not become a Status record.

rows.label: Reported value and associated uncertainty
rows.definition: A reported value and its optional error, preserving the native scalar type, quantity, units and stated uncertainty convention for each structure.

rows.boundary: Most Measured types explicitly require a plus/minus one-standard-deviation error convention. Count, Humidity, UTC and Measured Psecpm3 do not state that convention. Missing error is not zero or exactness; no conversion or normal-distribution assumption.

rows.label: Declared property definition
rows.definition: Named property contract with typing, structure and optional validity/publication rules.
display: Property Declaration: name, description, type, mutability, structure; range / threshold [0-1]
rows.boundary: Not a reported value, write permission for a particular caller, or current ready state.
rows.topics_source_review_boundary: Mutability labels describe how a reported property value can be changed, not the physical nature of a component, a guarantee of a supported actuation command or a universal authorization outcome.

rows.label: Declared observable definition
rows.definition: Observable contract; declared observables need not occur in every Event.
display: Observable Declaration: name, description, type, structure; range [0-1]
rows.boundary: The source says reported observables should be declared; do not strengthen should into shall. CMPT-M-0024/L-0068 separately uses shall for declaring all reportable/supported observables in the initial/included CCD. The DMS definition’s should wording remains preserved in its evidence; each modality is attributed to its source instead of silently substituting one for the other. Declared support still does not imply every Event contains the observable.
rows.topics_source_review_boundary: Event observables are observation-associated content; update-reference semantics and partial replacement differ from Config declarations and property Status values.

rows.label: Declared command interface
rows.definition: Supported command identity with parameter and result declarations.

rows.boundary: Declarations and readiness/reporting states remain distinct from current Status values and performed work. ICD7.3 says a modifiable property is marked mutable in the CCD; clearing it makes it Not Ready,and not-ready properties must be Not Reporting and absent from Status. The DMS Clear Property precondition remains a value previously supplied through Set Property; its null-value consequence is retained. This does not establish deletion of historical data or physical absence. IPL3 declaration representations do not change the saved DMS declaration contracts. CMPT requires initial Config within 30 seconds of ADDED. L-0058 includes the CCD and all false capability-state values; L-0061 includes the entire CCD when declarations change; L-0062 includes all false state values when states change and explicitly describes an empty state list when all states become true. This is not an arbitrary sparse patch rule or a universal Boolean default. Updates retain the source’s all-connected-components versus connected-Controller wording. Configuration updates have a 30-second send limit. M-0031 separately requires property changes after configuration-set changes; L-0082 ties its full reporting-true Status to an update Config containing a CCD, and L-0170 gives that full Status a 30-second limit. These source levels do not establish a full-Status trigger for every state-only update. On REVIVED, CMPT requires a complete configuration set and a Config send within30 seconds of the revival notification. This is recovery traffic, not evidence that configuration was accepted, deployed or physically realized. Controller Requirements 6.0r4: Controller initial Config mid-level received-first-Config and low-level outbound ADDED trigger wordings differ; updated Config carries only configuration-set changes, not Status property values.
rows.controller_source_review_boundary: Controller initial Config mid-level received-first-Config and low-level outbound ADDED trigger wordings differ; updated Config carries only configuration-set changes, not Status property values.
rows.controller_final_review_boundary: Live Data caches new Config information only if sufficient computing resources exist, transmits maintained matching Config on subscription creation and removes maintained Config on DEVICE REMOVED. This is not original source-history erasure.

rows.boundary: Distinct from a Get Status request, Config states and Event observables. ICD 6.5 gives general Status publication bounds through Minimum/Maximum Status Interval and contextual significant change. The saved DMS Threshold Declaration also specifies threshold publication regardless of status interval; retain both source statements without inventing precedence. IPL3 encodes standard properties as optional typed fields and custom properties through the named-value structure; list presence is separate from list contents. The DMS Status.properties list remains unchanged. CMPT initial Status includes every ready-and-reporting property and is due within 30 seconds of sending initial Config. Periodic Status includes all and only changed ready-and-reporting property values; a never-reported value is treated as changed. L-0093’s 500 ms response is conditional on a reporting-true property change after no periodic Status within the Minimum Status Interval, not a universal period. L-0082’s CCD-update Status instead says every reporting-true property; preserve that qualification difference. The saved Get Status command separately retrieves declared ready properties even when reporting is disabled. M-0037’s explanatory Note says these interval restrictions apply only to Status publication; the ICD separately reuses the named interval properties for command-response cadence. CMPT non-responsiveness recovery uses a500ms Status response. Higher-level text says full status, while L-0100 explicitly selects declared properties with ready=true and reporting=true; retain that source-level wording difference instead of silently broadening the message to every declared property. Controller Requirements 6.0r4: Initial Status mid-level and low-level triggers differ and have bounded timing; later Status carries changes only. Missed Status drives configurable network availability monitoring, not verified hardware failure.
rows.controller_source_review_boundary: Initial Status mid-level and low-level triggers differ and have bounded timing; later Status carries changes only. Missed Status drives configurable network availability monitoring, not verified hardware failure.
rows.controller_final_review_boundary: Live Data maintains new Status information only if resources permit, delivers matching maintained Status to new subscribers, removes maintained Status on DEVICE REMOVED and uses property changes to update subscription matching. It is not direct proof of physical health.
rows.topics_source_review_boundary: The guide describes general Resource Descriptors typically published as Status Resources; descriptive location/typed link is not evidence of a current reachable URL or actual component physical state.

rows.label: Registration message and credential data
rows.definition: Registration/deregistration information with operation, credentials and optional contextual error text.
rows.boundary: Registration.credentials is application-message data; it is distinct from the TLS certificate required by the ICD connection rules and the Certificate Guide trust/usage context. The saved DMS fields specify no automatic registration success or particular credential scheme. Possessing a certificate does not by itself establish a permitted command,successful registration or verified deployment security. CMPT-M-0018/L-0054 sends REQUEST ADD after successful format negotiation/Handshake Complete. M-0019 places the 30-second submission limit after successful negotiation; L-0055 says after establishing a connection. The connected-state Note and both anchors remain literal, without an invented reconciliation or a 30-second guarantee of successful admission. Controller Requirements 6.0r4: Controller responds with ERROR/ADDED after distinct authentication/authorization conditions within its 30-second limit, and REMOVED under separate deregistration rules; these are not physical equipment transitions.
rows.controller_source_review_boundary: Controller responds with ERROR/ADDED after distinct authentication/authorization conditions within its 30-second limit, and REMOVED under separate deregistration rules; these are not physical equipment transitions.
rows.controller_final_review_boundary: Authorization Service can evaluate Registration REQUEST ADD contents; this is separate from Controller-side certificate identity comparison, subsequent ADDED/ERROR registration and physical asset participation.

No invented identifier equality,conversion or executed exchange is claimed. CMPT-L-0144 repeats the explicit Response.reference=Request ID rule. Request uniqueness is the source UCI + request ID + time combination. These requirements reinforce correlation without collapsing Request.identifier, request id and message identity. Controller Requirements 6.0r4: The Controller forwards the Request to the cited performer or generates a PERMISSION DENIED Response. Previous DMS/ICD Request and Response reference semantics remain separately attributed.

rows.label: Requested message kinds and returned fields
rows.definition: A query identifies eligible message kinds and the desired content for each kind, separately from its Boolean match expression.
display: Data Query + Select → Administrative / Config / Event / Status Select
Requested message kinds and returned fields
rows.boundary: Named selection lists are Required 0+; optional priority/stale and Config ccd flags default false. Textual select status means all fields in the guide; do not equate omitted textual clauses with unpopulated object fields. The Position example also states a field-presence condition; do not generalize it to every selection. CMPT component discovery sends a Discover Request with the desired query to the targeted Live Data Service. When a Live Data Service recommendation was received, using it is should, not shall. This requirement does not change Data Query semantics or prove a discovery result.
rows.controller_final_review_boundary: Authorized valid Discover Request matches maintained Config/Status and reports SUCCESS even with zero matches; inability to perform matching is FAILED. Retrieval of stored Config/Status is distinct from performed sensing and real-time delivery.

rows.label: Message-matching criteria
rows.definition: Boolean criteria combine child predicates or compare left and right values with one of six sealed comparator codes.
display: Match → And / Or / Not / Boolean Match / Boolean Function / Boolean Wrapper; Comparator
rows.boundary: And/Or require one or more inputs; Not has exactly one. Preserve the guide grammar rather than assuming familiar operator precedence. XOR-to-object translation is not supplied. exists() literally returns true for an empty value; no silent inversion.
rows.controller_final_review_boundary: Discovery and subscription filtering use source-defined maintained Config/Status and newly received Config/Status/Event/Administrative messages. Property changes may start or stop matching; no universal query syntax or inferred current measurement is added.

rows.label: Field navigation and contextual filtering
rows.definition: A selector starts from a value context or named field, applies an optional predicate and can descend through additional fields.
display: Value Selector.context / predicate / field selection; Field Value Selector.field / predicate / field selection
rows.boundary: False predicates remove the current object or node from context. Recursive paths are query navigation, not physical composition. Retain the grammar distinction between field and explicit-context selectors.

rows.label: Query functions and arguments
rows.definition: A named function call supplies an empty-capable argument list and produces either a Boolean match result or a value; declared parameters pair names and values.
display: Boolean Function / Value Function.name + arguments; Function Parameter.name + value
rows.boundary: Function names do not establish commands or executable equipment controls. The grammar permits positional as well as named arguments; the guide does not specify how unnamed arguments populate required Function Parameter.name.

rows.label: Literal and list query values
rows.definition: Query operands can be static values, lists, function results or values obtained by contextual field selection.
display: Value → Field Value Selector / List Value / Static Value / Value Function / Value Selector
rows.boundary: List Value contains Value[0+]; Static Value contains exactly one Wildcard. Retain misleading battlefield-entity prose without converting these query containers into an entity model. concat and unique describe list operations, not observation fusion.

rows.label: String matching rules
rows.definition: The DMS defines a restricted glob-style string comparison, while the guide separately describes a regular-expression Boolean function.
display: String Match: case-sensitive / exact-match / pattern; DQL regexp(pattern, subject)
rows.boundary: String Match recognizes only *, ? and backslash as special pattern characters; exact-match describes boundary anchors. It is not a listed Match union alternative and is not assumed equivalent to regexp() or an unrestricted regular-expression engine.

rows.label: Subscription identity and query definition
rows.definition: A subscription pairs its Data Query with a structured identifier containing the creator, consumer and name.
display: Subscription.query + id; Subscription ID.creator / consumer / name
Related only · Publish-subscribe and topic identity · §15.6.4 · RELATED BUT DIFFERENT [SOSA-D ledger]
rows.boundary: All five fields across the two structures are required single values. The identifier is not just a label or number. Keep subscription description distinct from Add/Remove Subscription requests and from evidence that delivery actually occurred. CMPT Add Subscription requests carry desired filters and a locally unique name; Remove Subscription cites the subscription ID and the Live Data Service instance where the subscription was created. Recommended Live Data Service use is should. Definition, command exchange and delivered subscription data remain distinct. Controller Requirements 6.0r4: Controller notification 'for distribution to subscribers' does not redefine subscription identity, prove receipt or assert permanent source-record deletion.
rows.controller_source_review_boundary: Controller notification 'for distribution to subscribers' does not redefine subscription identity, prove receipt or assert permanent source-record deletion.
rows.controller_final_review_boundary: Creation includes consumer identity/filter and returns unique subscription ID; creator and consumer may differ. Maintenance while creator registered and cleanup on removed consumer are separately worded; matched messages go to consumer.

rows.label: Subscription selection and initial-cache options
rows.definition: Options govern inclusion of the subscriber’s own messages, exact type comparison and whether initial subscription results include cached values.
display: Data Query.with clause / without clause; loopback; strictcomparisons / strictcomparison; without cache
rows.boundary: The guide spells the strict option differently in prose and examples; neither spelling is silently chosen as implementation truth. without cache concerns initial returned context, not deletion of cached data, a ban on cached lookup functions or archival History semantics.
rows.controller_final_review_boundary: New subscriptions receive maintained matching Config and Status as specified by Controller Requirements; earlier DQL initial-cache options remain separately sourced. This is not an Event history cache or proof of universal initial cache behavior.

rows.label: Message-source and cached-component query context
rows.definition: Queries distinguish message source from the component being described and can consult cached component messages during matching.
display: source(); component(); get_config(); get_status(); get_administrative(); get_event()
rows.boundary: component() uses Administrative About UCIs. Cached lookups use source, or About for Administrative context. Events are not cached: get_event returns the active Event or an empty list. These functions are not Get Config/Get Status command execution.
rows.controller_final_review_boundary: Maintained Config/Status and newly received Event detector properties affect query/subscription context; detector properties in an Event do not become component Status reports.

rows.label: Spatial component and message selection
rows.definition: Spatial functions return component UCIs or test a message against a geographic ellipse or polygon, with an explicit positionless-target option.
rows.boundary: The near-UCI function defaults minor axis to major axis, rotation to zero and positionless inclusion to false. in_area distinguishes source positions, Administrative About components and Event detection area/position. No coordinates, distance interpretation or common position semantics are invented from an example.

rows.boundary: Six DMS service definitions are not six mandatory Controller modules. SDD 4.2.1 requires each ISA 6.0 Controller to support all three core services, while support and activation are distinct; 5.0 separately describes typical hosting. Any component may provide optional services. Empty property/observable columns do not prohibit additional capabilities. Support, activation, provider selection, authorization, request, execution and achieved effects remain separate. CMPT service recommendations are conditional on needing a service. Set Live Data Service and Set Authorization Service support is likewise conditional; recommendation receipt does not prove activation, provider binding or successful service use. Controller Requirements 6.0r4: Three mandatory Controller core services differ from best-available service recommendation, authorized Request forwarding and Event forwarding; none establishes actual provider acceptance or execution.
rows.controller_source_review_boundary: Three mandatory Controller core services differ from best-available service recommendation, authorized Request forwarding and Event forwarding; none establishes actual provider acceptance or execution.
rows.controller_final_review_boundary: Authorization determines permissions; Live Data maintains conditional Config/Status discovery state and routes subscribed messages. Required source service behaviors do not establish their deployed performance or hardware classes.

rows.boundary: Required lists two interval properties and seven commands; Recommended lists Identity, Operating State, Clear Property and Set Property. This is a source obligation, not a test result or a claim that any case component conforms. Retain must versus should. The DMS baseline remains two required properties and seven required commands. CMPT §4.1.3 separately recommends Identity and Operating State, makes Set Observable Reporting conditional on publishing observables, and requires Set Property for settable properties. Its READ WRITE note does not erase the DMS WRITE ONLY value. Conditional shall and should retain their stated scope; no case-component conformance is inferred.

rows.label: Externally visible member taskability
rows.definition: For a member visible outside a composition, the CIC separately determines whether external tasking of that member is enabled.
display: Visible + tasking enabled = transparent; visible + tasking not enabled = translucent; only visible members can be targeted externally
rows.boundary: Visibility, declared support, taskability, requester authorization, execution and successful effects are separate. Figure 2 labels incoming Member B tasks although B is translucent; only C has a forwarded task arrow. Preserve that tension without inventing task forwarding to or execution by B.

rows.label: Composition interface task mediation role
rows.definition: For a received external task, the CIC may perform the task itself, actively task members, or forward the request to a selected member.
display: CIC per-request role: performer executes; broker actively tasks members; relay forwards via ISA or native member interface

rows.label: Capability readiness and reporting selection
rows.definition: A declared capability has a ready state, and a reporting capability has a separate reporting selection. The meaning of readiness depends on whether the capability is a command, property or observable.
display: Command ready = execution enabled; property ready = value maintained; observable ready = recording enabled; property/observable reporting selects publication

Related only · Direct versus delegated indirect management / In-band versus out-of-band management / Sta… · §6 printed38/PDF64 · RELATED BUT DIFFERENT [SOSA-D ledger] · G2-2: PICs may be unmanaged, directly managed or indirectly represented; source Rule labels duplicate and no device readiness is established · G2-3: §6.5 System Manager-assessed PIC/module operational vs communications-lost state, not enabled capability · G2-4B: MORA getDeviceStatus and configurable status update interval concern reported RF device state · G2-6A: PSC FAIL* and ENABLE*/INHIBIT* specify electrical fault/output logic · G2-6D: Legacy status concerns profile inclusion in standards, not current hardware operation · G2-7A: Slash and colon encode configurable versus auto-negotiated design alternatives · G2-7B: E18~ is a dormant electrical physical-port example · G2-7C: C239 matrix X/legacy and illustrative protocol selections concern design/reference standing · G2-7F: Rule4 describes required implementability of configurable physical multi-protocol ports.
rows.boundary: CMPT-L-0072–0081 and their explanatory Notes distinguish command enablement from immediate availability, property maintenance/access on request from publication, and observable recording enablement from inclusion in Events. A ready command may still be busy. These states do not establish authorization, execution, an observed physical effect or a measured hardware-health condition. Config false-state-list rules are source-specific message semantics, not invented defaults for every required Boolean. Saved DMS Command/Property/Observable State definitions and their wording notes remain intact. Observation publication includes only ready-and-reporting observables. Command requests are limited to declared commands whose ready state is true, yet a ready command can still be temporarily unavailable, queued or BUSY. Reporting/readiness/request eligibility and immediate execution remain separate. Controller Requirements 6.0r4: Service recommendation depends on a received Config declaring the relevant Set ISA ... Service command. Capability declaration, current readiness, provider selection and successful service use remain distinct.
rows.controller_source_review_boundary: Service recommendation depends on a received Config declaring the relevant Set ISA ... Service command. Capability declaration, current readiness, provider selection and successful service use remain distinct.

rows.boundary: ICD6.0r5 supports IPL protocol version1 and lists Protocol Buffers/XML long and short forms plus0x05/0x01 Custom Java API encoding. Unsupported/deprecated format pairs and inconsistent printed examples retain their source standing. IPL3 transforms standard capabilities into dedicated declarations/fields/request types while custom content retains generic structures. Neither IPL Format3 nor its schema byte is protocol version3. No actual negotiation,schema-file validation or current security result is asserted. CMPT-L-0042/0043 requires all supported ICD formats in preference order; it adds no Controller selection rule. L-0048 requires the smallest suitable application-data wrapper, while the ICD describes best fit with should. L-0046/0051/0052 require the stated early-data, invalid-type and decode-failure errors. The Sensor CE Format 3 sentence is an explanatory Note, not a universal format mandate. Negotiation completion permits IPL data exchange subject to the later ISA participation restrictions. Controller Requirements 6.0r4: Controller selects a supported IPL format from the sorted offer and reports unsupported formats; the explicit may begin application exchange differs from a mandatory send. Preserve ICD edition boundaries.

rows.label: Supplied list value versus no update
rows.definition: The presence of a supplied collection value is distinct from the collection contents,so an explicit empty value can be distinguished from an omitted update.
display: IPL3 list-based property/observable: associated *_supplied Boolean; true marks the list as provided,including an empty list
Supplied list value versus no update
rows.boundary: IPL3 says absent and empty lists otherwise encode alike and adds presence Booleans to Status/Event for list-based properties and observables. True indicates the associated value is supplied even when empty. The guide does not specify defaults for false or omitted flags,wire tags or an authorization decision; it does not prescribe this mechanism for every DMS list or erase list bounds/history.

rows.label: Component time basis and synchronization
rows.definition: A component has a time reference, synchronization approach and epoch underlying the times it communicates, separately from the meaning of an Event occurrence time or an exchange transmission time.

rows.boundary: CMPT-H-0004 requires UTC synchronization and L-0032 states the UNIX epoch. M-0010 uses shall for NTP synchronization, with a Note allowing GPS; L-0031 uses should and calls NTP a design goal. Preserve those levels and the source definition that Notes are explanatory. Epoch does not determine timestamp units or collapse occurrence and transmission times; saved UTC/time type definitions retain their own rules.

individual_correspondences.why: SOSA Sensor contributes a specific sensor-system boundary and modality to the proposed described sensing arrangement.
individual_correspondences.guard: Does not prove generic CSAPI System identity, ownership of deployed sensors or a mandatory domain superclass.

individual_correspondences.why: Source's generic System/SubSystem concept permits hierarchical systems without fixing one sensing domain root.
individual_correspondences.guard: Generic SOSA System is not always an instantiated physical sensing apparatus.

individual_correspondences.why: A SOSA Hardware Element is physical and can be a sensor constituent, with source-defined configuration bounds.
individual_correspondences.guard: Not every physical environmental probe or other equipment is a SOSA hardware element.

individual_correspondences.why: PIC, aperture, chassis/enclosure and power supply are documented SOSA hardware/infrastructure examples.
individual_correspondences.guard: SOSA hardware architecture is not universal sensor hardware inventory or mandatory chassis hierarchy.

individual_correspondences.why: SOSA Host Platform contributes concrete physical support/mounting context for a SOSA Sensor.
individual_correspondences.guard: Does not establish source-specific geolocation, site operator, sensor's own geometry or a software host.

individual_correspondences.why: SOSA Sensor Pod is an integral packaging and mounting case where sensor and pod boundaries overlap.
individual_correspondences.guard: Cannot always treat pod as external hosting platform or as a physically separate sensor.

individual_correspondences.why: SOSA External Interface crosses sensor boundary and may connect to host/environment.
individual_correspondences.guard: Not equivalent to a distinct externally cabled ClimaVue, SDI-12 connector, or all connected equipment.

individual_correspondences.why: Internal interfaces and drawn physical relationships provide relation/context evidence.
individual_correspondences.guard: Interface presence does not entail strict part-of, one function per card or installed topology.

individual_correspondences.why: SOSA Module is a separately defined functional architecture role that might be implemented on physical hardware.
individual_correspondences.guard: It must NOT be read as physical constituent by label or produce phantom hardware/part-of edges.

individual_correspondences.why: SOSA Sensor Component and generic Element can include logical/software as well as physical realizations.
individual_correspondences.guard: Cannot silently equate 'component' with physical module, installed probe or hardware individual.

individual_correspondences.why: RTE describes execution hosting of software, not a physical vehicle/structure.
individual_correspondences.guard: Do not use unqualified platform/host terms to infer location or physical attachment.

individual_correspondences.why: Interaction infrastructure carries logical information exchange between modules.
individual_correspondences.guard: Transport/binding cannot prove a distinct network-visible node, physical cable or original measurement author.

individual_correspondences.why: A procurable unit may implement multiple modules/physical infrastructure elements.
individual_correspondences.guard: Purchase unit or product type is not identical to one module, one model designation, one installed asset or one sensor.
